clue.text: Depression over rotten clue

indicators.note: over in an across clue signals the word for depression is turned round

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: A slump in mood brought on by a puzzle clue that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood but is a hollow in the ground, turned round by 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint or piece of advance information is a clue, as in a racing or police tip.

clue.text: Shot hit bull

indicators.note: hit suggests the word has been struck and knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shot at a dartboard that strikes the bullseye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' rearranges SHOT. 'Bull' here is short for nonsense, not the centre of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for rubbish talk, and this British word means nonsense too.

clue.text: Dangerous source of infestation, briefly substandard?

parts.note: read as sub standard: the standard, par, set under what follows; in a down clue the lower piece comes second

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasite that infests hair and bedding

explanation.surface: A dodgy hint that something is infested and below par.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'substandard' as 'sub' (under) and 'standard' (PAR): LOUS, the shortened LOUSE, sits under PAR in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous is an old-fashioned synonym for perilous, full of danger or uncertainty.

clue.text: Off-key band to assemble at home

parts.note: a note sung below pitch is flat
a pack is a group or band, as of wolves

explanation.surface: A tuneless group of musicians getting together at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assembly furniture sold in boxed parts is built by the buyer in their own house.

clue.text: She opposes men on purpose

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the word for men after the word for purpose

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A woman who deliberately stands against the men.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises protests is a dissenter; 'she' here is one such person.

clue.text: Scrounge child's food for theatre audiences

parts.note: to bum is to cadge or scrounge
a son is a child; with the 's it gives SONS
eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: Cadging a youngster's snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's' supplies SON plus the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that pulls in paying spectators is said to put this many people in the stalls, an idiom for audience numbers.

clue.text: Essex opener run out twice in fourth match

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for run; two of them are taken out

parts.note: a quarter is one fourth

explanation.surface: Cricket: an Essex batsman is run out twice in the fourth game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out twice' removes both Rs from QUARTER, leaving QUATE. Essex is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: To match two things is to treat them as equal, or make them balance.

clue.text: Current actor finally stops playing Hamlet

indicators.note: stops is read as plugs: the letter fills a gap in the rearranged word
playing suggests the word is performed loosely, so its letters are rearranged
finally picks out the last letter

explanation.surface: An actor at last quits his run in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns HAMLET into THEMAL; 'stops' puts R, from 'actor finally', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of warm air is a current that gliders and birds ride upward.

clue.text: Official seat DIY centres supply, when temperature's dropped

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
dropped means the temperature letter is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Home-improvement stores provide something, once the heat is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' rearranges DIY CENTRES and 'dropped' takes T out of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A residency is the official house of a governor or diplomat, so an official seat.

clue.text: Charge almost certain to prove trying

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
to tax someone is to try or strain them

explanation.surface: A charge that is all but guaranteed to be tested.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra levy on high incomes is a type of fiscal charge.

clue.text: People like Nelson meet up as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fans of Nelson gathering as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Nelson lost his right arm in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson lost an arm, so he is an example of someone who has had a limb removed.

clue.text: Proceed unsteadily round bed, muffling soft sound

indicators.note: unsteadily suggests a wobble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sea or river bed is its bottom; round says the shaken letters end up wrapped about it
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft; muffling says the shaken letters wrap it up too

explanation.surface: Walking shakily around a bed while stifling a quiet noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' wants to be a noise beside 'soft'; it is the definition, meaning secure. 'muffling' takes the soft letter into the pool that 'unsteadily' shakes up, and 'round' wraps that around the bed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper-sheathed ship's hull is reliable, so the word means thoroughly trustworthy or safe.

clue.text: Policy Americans go wild for

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A political programme that US citizens love.
explanation.walkthrough: The economics of US President Ronald Reagan.
explanation.definitionFit: The supply-side economic programme of the 1980s US government was a named policy.

clue.text: Old coach is last to leave, following after tea

indicators.note: following means what comes next is placed after the tea

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A former trainer is the final one to go, after afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer; it is a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed four-wheeled carriage pulled by hired horses was a form of transport in the 18th century.

clue.text: Record of suffering that can be glossed over?

parts.note: pain means suffering
a table is a record of figures

explanation.surface: A list of hardships that can be conveniently skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glossed over' is read literally: covered with gloss paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface fit to take a coat of gloss is one a decorator can brush with colour.

clue.text: Manx side filled case

indicators.note: the Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a flank is a side

explanation.surface: A side from the Isle of Man filled a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry shell holding a sweet or savoury filling is this open tart.

clue.text: Special ingredient's moreish, but calorie-free!

indicators.note: free here means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: something moreish makes you want more, so it is addictive
C is the abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A diet food's secret component is irresistible yet contains no calories.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put into food to improve colour or flavour is a supplementary ingredient.

clue.text: This is not Long Island

definitions.meaning: a tiny unit of length, only about two and a half centimetres, is hardly long
in Scotland and Ireland a small island is called by this name

explanation.surface: Pretends to be a remark about some place other than Long Island, New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A short measure of length and a Scottish word for an islet.

clue.text: Announcement in Daily Express leader elicits mockery

indicators.note: in means the announcement sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaner who comes in each day

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is an announcement

explanation.surface: A notice in a British tabloid's editorial provokes ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British newspaper; a 'daily' is also a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a pretence or travesty, a farce that mocks the real thing.

clue.text: Note: wife's ignoring country custom to a great extent

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter is left out

parts.note: Rwanda is an African country
a way is a custom or habit

explanation.surface: A memo: a wife disregards rural traditions on a large scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country custom' reads as rural tradition, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means by a long way, very much indeed.

clue.text: Cunning plans asthmatics produce?

definitions.meaning: a British slang word for clever schemes or tricks
breathless people make whistling sounds as they breathe

explanation.surface: Clever schemes cooked up by breathless people.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemes or dodges in British slang, and rasping breaths in plain English.

clue.text: Neatening piece of frayed gingham?

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tidying up a ragged bit of checked cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming a border neatly, as with a lawn or hem, tidies it.

clue.text: Proprietor adds rent for skilled weaver

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord adds rent to the bill of a craftsman at the loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: This creature spins silk to build a burrow with a hinged lid, a skilful web-maker.

clue.text: Conservative PM to go Liberal?

parts.note: to go is a coy euphemism for urinating, as in needing to go

explanation.surface: Could a Tory prime minister defect to the Liberals?
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Conservative prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Peel led the Conservative government twice in the 1830s and 1840s.

clue.text: Intimate clothing troubles holding one back in capital

parts.note: a bra is underwear

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
holding means the word wraps around the letter

parts.note: ails means troubles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Underwear problems keep someone from getting ahead in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside AILS to make AILIS, and 'back' turns that into SILIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The planned city in Brazil's interior has been that country's seat of government since 1960.

clue.text: They say pop will die, having promised much

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: pop is fizz, and will contracts to 'll, so spoken it is fizz'll

explanation.surface: Pundits predict a pop act will flop despite the hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' means the contraction FIZZ'LL is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A firework that hisses and goes out has a disappointing end, like a promising venture that peters out.

clue.text: Motivate soldier in deceptively serene setting

indicators.note: in places the soldier within the rearranged letters
deceptively means the letters are not what they appear and must be rearranged

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier rousing others in a setting that only seems peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deceptively' turns SERENE into ENERSE, with GI placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone vigour and drive is to stimulate or galvanise them.

clue.text: Pull gently on large plant

parts.note: to tease fibres or hair is to pull them gently apart

explanation.surface: Gently tugging on a big shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiny heads of this plant were once used to raise the nap on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly plant with burr-like heads used to comb cloth; a member of the plant kingdom.
